children: Takuto Kimura says the company plans to introduce new locally manufactured watch models in 2027 as it seeks to double women’s watch sales by expanding its product portfolio

Casio India sees scope to double women’s watch sales by expanding its locally manufactured portfolio, developing new models across watch categories and capitalising on demand for fashion-led timepieces. The Japanese watchmaker is also looking to strengthen its brand presence and widen its retail reach, including in smaller cities and banking on demand for traditional watches among younger consumers.

“We will especially try to focus on increasing the Make in India line-ups and focus on the women's line-up…if we strengthen our strategy and product line-up in the women market, I'm confident that we can increase the sales double,” Takuto Kimura, Managing Director, Casio India, said in an interview with BW Businessworld on the sidelines of the Launch of G-Shock 2500 series.

The company has not disclosed the current contribution of women's watches to its Indian sales, a timeline for doubling the segment's sales or a quantified investment plan. Kimura said strengthening the product range and market strategy would be central to pursuing the opportunity, with additional India-made models potentially arriving in 2027.

Casio introduced a range of 28 locally manufactured watch models in January 2026, including 23 designs aimed at women, according to previously reported company announcements. The next phase of product development could include additions under G-Shock and Edifice, and other segments also, although the company has not confirmed launch dates or the number of models planned.

Casio reported double-digit sales growth for both G-Shock and its Casio Watch brand. Its results briefing said Casio Watch attracted new users, including women and younger consumers, and identified marketing to women as part of its strategy. The company also said demand for smartwatches appeared to have passed its peak.

Additionally, Casio India's revenue more than doubled to Rs 894 crore in FY25 from Rs 394 crore in FY21, while net profit rose to Rs 53.6 crore from Rs 8.3 crore over the same period, according to regulatory filings accessed through business intelligence platform Tofler.
Traditional Watches Remain Priority

Casio India is not currently planning to enter the smartwatch segment, despite the category's earlier rapid expansion. Kimura said the company would continue to focus on traditional watches, keeping its domestic strategy centred on established product categories rather than adding smartwatch offerings.
“As of now we focus on traditional watch,” Kimura said.

India's smartwatch market has contracted for two consecutive years, according to International Data Corporation (IDC). Shipments fell 17.6 per cent to 28.9 million units in 2025. In April-June 2026, shipments declined 4 per cent to 6.38 million units, marking the tenth consecutive quarter of contraction, although the decline was narrower than the 28.4 per cent fall recorded a year earlier.

The slowdown has not been uniform across the wider watch industry. Titan Company reported 23 per cent growth in its watches division in the June quarter of FY27, according to its business update. Analogue watches grew in the high twenties, while its smartwatch business declined in the low teens, highlighting the contrasting performance of traditional and connected timepieces.
“The young generation in India more tends to have a watch. Not only just timekeeping but also they try to wear it to express their own style and fashion,” he said.

He identified G-Shock as a brand that resonates with younger consumers who follow global trends in fashion, art, music and sport through social media. Casio Vintage, meanwhile, has benefited from interest in 1990s fashion, he said.

In India, Casio attributed continued G-Shock growth partly to the impact of two major brand ambassadors. Sales of Casio Watch also remained strong as its distributor network expanded beyond major cities into smaller urban markets. India and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations together accounted for 16 per cent of Casio's timepiece sales in the quarter; the company did not provide a separate India figure.
Casio India's immediate priorities remain watches, calculators and electronic musical instruments. Kimura said the company had no current plans to launch its earU hearing-assistance earbuds in India.
Retail Expansion Across India

Alongside product development, Casio India plans to increase its physical retail presence and strengthen online sales. The company had 85 brand stores at the time of the interview, Kimura said, as it seeks to build its reach across major cities and smaller markets. The company has a target to open 200 stores by 2030 and, with the ambition to double its India business over five years, Shin Takano, the company’s global CEO, has said previously.

“One of the key strategies we have to focus on is how to increase the number of brand stores nationwide in India…So from tier 1, we try to open a new flagship brand store. And tier 2, we expand the number of brand stores,” Kimura said, adding that while continuing to consider opportunities in tier 3 cities. At the same time, online sales would remain another area of focus.

Kimura said online and offline sales of watches were broadly comparable, although he did not provide a detailed channel-wise breakdown or distinguish between sales through Casio's own website and third-party ecommerce platforms.

In a September 2025, Kimura said Casio held a 12 per cent share of India's watch market, ranking second, compared with 8 per cent in 2014. He also outlined an ambition to triple sales by 2035. These figures were company-reported claims and were not independently established in the latest interview.
Competition In Women's Watches

Men's watches account for an estimated 57.68 per cent of India's watch market, while women's watches are the fastest-growing segment, with estimated growth of 9.16 per cent, according to Mordor Intelligence. The figures point to an opportunity for brands to broaden their appeal among women, although the estimates depend on the research firm's market definitions and forecast period.

Casio India is looking to strengthen its presence in the segment through product development and local manufacturing. Its women's portfolio will span categories including G-Shock and Edifice, Kimura said, as the company seeks to address a gap in its existing range.
“I think the women's category, of course some other brands have more line-up than Casio. However, as I said, the women market now has a big potential, so we strengthen this market,” he said.

Casio faces competition from established watchmakers and brands with dedicated women's collections. Titan's Raga range, alongside offerings from Fossil and Citizen, gives consumers alternatives designed around women's styling preferences. Casio's challenge is to expand its range and strengthen its relevance in a segment where competitors already have established product offerings.

Kimura said Indian consumers consider both price and brand value when choosing watches, although the importance of price varies across market segments. Casio's strategy is to build brand recognition through marketing while pricing products to suit their intended consumers. He did not provide a breakdown of sales or profitability for women's watches.
Priyanshu Priya
BW Reporters The author is trainee correspondent at BW Businessworld.
